# Common networking surface area

Scope: the behavior that every network driver must have, and the Engine API requests for networks
and endpoints that do not depend on the network's driver. This spec describes them as observable
from outside the daemon.

This spec holds expectations that every network driver shares. It is not yet a complete account.
[../README.md](../README.md) gives the model that this spec follows: the items of a spec, their
categories and what their verdicts depend on. [README.md](README.md) gives the conventions of the
networking specs, such as vantage points, daemon settings, timing and convergence ceilings, and host
requirements. [swarm-networking.md](swarm-networking.md) and [bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md) cover what is specific to their drivers. [ipvlan-networking.md](ipvlan-networking.md) covers the ipvlan driver. The macvlan driver has no spec of its own, and its
expectations are here. [container-dns.md](container-dns.md) covers name resolution.

In this spec, a predefined network is a network that `GET /networks` with the filter
`type=builtin` lists. On a manager, the Swarm also has two Swarm-scoped networks named
`bridge` and `host`, whose `Labels` include
`com.docker.swarm.predefined`: the Swarm's predefined networks. A service that names
`bridge` or `host` refers to one of them, and its tasks use the node's own network
of that name. The filter `type=builtin` does not list them, so they are not predefined
networks in the sense of this spec. `GET /networks` does not list them at all
([*SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED*](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED)). A lookup by name without `scope` `swarm`
does not match them ([*NET-API-INSPECT-NAME-SWARM-PREDEFINED*](#NET-API-INSPECT-NAME-SWARM-PREDEFINED)), so an expectation that says
that a name matches more than one network does not count them. The expectations here also hold for
Swarm-scoped networks and on nodes in a Swarm, unless an expectation's own text says otherwise.
[Network lifecycle & API surface](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface) in [swarm-networking.md](swarm-networking.md) covers the requests that are specific to Swarm-scoped networks.

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/#versioned-api-and-sdk; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/#minimum-api-version

*Refines:* [PRIN-STABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-STABLE) · *Refined by:* [NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION), [NET-IFACE-NAME-PATTERN](#NET-IFACE-NAME-PATTERN), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED-WINDOWS](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED-WINDOWS), [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE), [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-API-VERSION](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-API-VERSION), [SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR-WINDOWS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR-WINDOWS), [SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU-WINDOWS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU-WINDOWS), [SWARM-PUB-UNKNOWN-PROTOCOL](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PUB-UNKNOWN-PROTOCOL), [SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-CREATE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-CREATE) · *Violated by:* [NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT-API-VERSION](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT-API-VERSION)

responses are adjusted to the API version that the client uses.

names, responds with a 4xx status. The exception is a refusal that another requirement promises
status 501 for, such as an ingress network with a driver other than overlay.

<a id="REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM**: A ConfigFrom network takes its configuration from a config-only network

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkCreate; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#swarm-networks-with-local-scope-drivers

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-ADDRESSES](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-ADDRESSES), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-IPAM](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-IPAM), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CLI](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CLI), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-WRONG-KIND](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-WRONG-KIND), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-ATTACHED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-ATTACHED), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-SUBNET](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-SUBNET) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE)

ConfigFrom names the source of a network's configuration, which must be an existing config-only
network. The network then uses that network's configuration, such as its subnets and gateway.

<a id="REQ-NET-CONFIG-ONLY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CONFIG-ONLY**: A config-only network holds configuration and cannot run containers

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkCreate; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#swarm-networks-with-local-scope-drivers

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-CLI](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING-CLI), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CREATE](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CREATE), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-SERVICE](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-SERVICE), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START-CLI](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START-CLI)

A network created with ConfigOnly is a placeholder whose configuration other networks use. It
cannot be used directly to run containers or services.

<a id="REQ-NET-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-IN-USE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-IN-USE**: A config-only network that another network uses cannot be removed

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/libnetwork/pull/1742: the commit that adds configuration networks

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-USED](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-USED), [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-USED-CLI](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-USED-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-REFUSED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-REFUSED), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-REFUSED-CLI](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-REFUSED-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-UNUSED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-UNUSED)

A config-only network can be removed once no other network uses it, and not before.

<a id="REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE**: A failed connect or start leaves the container's networks as they were

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52480: a merged fix and its stated intent

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED](#NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED), [NET-API-START-FAILED-ENDPOINT-NOT-LISTED](#NET-API-START-FAILED-ENDPOINT-NOT-LISTED), [NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT](#NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT)

A failed connect drops the NetworkSettings.Networks entry that it added. A start that fails at
network setup keeps the container's networks from container create, and the next start fails too
while the cause of the failure holds. The container list then reports no endpoint from the
failed attempt.

<a id="REQ-NET-CONNECT-ONCE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CONNECT-ONCE**: A network cannot be connected again to a running container

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkConnect

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED), [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-CLI](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-CLI)

POST /networks/{id}/connect cannot re-attach a network to a running container that is already
attached to it.

<a id="REQ-NET-CONNECT-REPEAT-STOPPED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CONNECT-REPEAT-STOPPED**: A repeat connect of a stopped container succeeds

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Scripts and unit files that connect a stopped container to its networks before each start (such as a systemd ExecStartPre that runs docker network connect on every boot). The API reference refuses a repeat connect only for a running container

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED), [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-CLI](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-CLI)

POST /networks/{id}/connect for a created or stopped container that already has the network
succeeds, and the container keeps the network.

<a id="REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS**: Container create accepts several networks from API 1.44

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v144-api-changes

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS), [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-CLI](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-CLI), [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED)

From API version 1.44, POST /containers/create accepts more than one network in
NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig; earlier API versions accept one.

<a id="REQ-NET-DAEMON-JSON-KEYS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-DAEMON-JSON-KEYS**: A daemon.json key sets the same option as the dockerd flag of its name

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/dockerd/#daemon-configuration-file

*Refined by:* [BR-OPT-DAEMON-MTU-APPLIED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-DAEMON-MTU-APPLIED) · *Violated by:* [BR-OPT-DAEMON-MTU-ZERO-REPLACED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-DAEMON-MTU-ZERO-REPLACED)

A daemon.json key that is the name of a dockerd flag, or the plural of the name of a flag that
allows several entries, sets the same option as that flag, and a value means the same in the
file as on the command line. Keys that are not named after a flag are not covered.

<a id="REQ-NET-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ATTACHMENT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ATTACHMENT**: A container run without a network is connected to the default bridge

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#differences-between-user-defined-bridges-and-the-default-bridge; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#connect-a-container-to-the-default-bridge-network

*Refined by:* [BR-EGRESS-UNDERLAY-REACH](bridge-networking.md#BR-EGRESS-UNDERLAY-REACH), [BR-ISO-SAME-NETWORK](bridge-networking.md#BR-ISO-SAME-NETWORK), [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-DEFAULT-BRIDGE) · *Violates:* [PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS](../principles.md#PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS)

On Linux, a container that is run without a network is connected to the default bridge network.
Containers on the default bridge can communicate with each other by IP address, and have access
to network services outside the host.

<a id="REQ-NET-DELETE-IN-USE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-DELETE-IN-USE**: A network with connected containers cannot be removed

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/rm/; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/ls/#filter

*Refined by:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE), [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI)

To remove a network, its containers must first be disconnected from it; removing a network that
has containers attached fails.

<a id="REQ-NET-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-DISCONNECT**: A container can be disconnected, and connected or disconnected while stopped

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/disconnect/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/prior-releases/#1100-2016-02-04

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED), [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-CLI](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-CLI), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-CLI](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-CLI), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-IFACE](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-IFACE), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED-CLI](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED-CLI) · *Violated by:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT)

docker network disconnect removes a container from a network. Connect and disconnect also work
on stopped containers.

<a id="REQ-NET-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED**: A disconnect from a network the container is not on fails

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/44151: a report that maintainers triaged and that expects the error

*Refined by:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-CLI](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-CLI)

A request to disconnect a container from a network that it is not attached to fails with an
error.

<a id="REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS**: An endpoint MacAddress sets the container's MAC address on the network

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkConnect; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v144-api-changes; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v154-api-changes; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#network

*Refined by:* [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION)

EndpointSettings.MacAddress sets the endpoint's MAC address on container create from API 1.44,
and on network connect from API 1.54. At earlier API versions, each of these requests ignores
the field.

<a id="REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY**: The endpoint with the highest gw-priority gives the default gateway

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#connecting-to-multiple-networks; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v148-api-changes; api/openapi.yaml: definition EndpointSettings (GwPriority)

*Refined by:* [NET-GW-PRIORITY](#NET-GW-PRIORITY), [NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT), [NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE), [NET-GW-PRIORITY-TIE](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-TIE)

The network whose endpoint has the highest gw-priority (default 0) provides the container's
default gateway, on create and on connect. Container create and network connect accept
GwPriority from API 1.48. Among endpoints with the same priority, one with both an IPv4 and an
IPv6 gateway comes before one with a gateway for a single address family, and remaining ties go
to the network name that sorts first. Each address family takes its default gateway from the
first endpoint in that order that has one.

<a id="REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS**: ExtraHosts entries are added to the container's hosts file

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* api/openapi.yaml: definition HostConfig (ExtraHosts); https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#add-host

*Refined by:* [NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS](#NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS), [NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI](#NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI) · *Violated by:* [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

HostConfig.ExtraHosts lists hostname to IP address mappings, in the form hostname:IP, to add to
the container's /etc/hosts file. docker run --add-host adds such an entry.

<a id="REQ-NET-HOST-GATEWAY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-HOST-GATEWAY**: host-gateway resolves to the host-gateway addresses

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/dockerd/#configure-host-gateway-ip; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#add-host; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/28/#2800

*Refined by:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY), [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE)

An --add-host value of host-gateway resolves to addresses of the host: by default the default
bridge's IPv4 address and its IPv6 address if it has one, or the addresses set with
host-gateway-ips.

<a id="REQ-NET-HOSTS-FQDN"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-HOSTS-FQDN**: A dotted hostname gives full and short names in /etc/hosts

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/29100: a report of the missing short name that maintainers agreed was a bug and fixed

*Refined by:* [NET-HOSTS-DOMAIN-NAME](#NET-HOSTS-DOMAIN-NAME)

When a container's hostname is a fully qualified name, its /etc/hosts line has both the full
name and the unqualified name.

<a id="REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME**: A container's /etc/hosts maps its addresses to its hostname

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#custom-hosts

*Refined by:* [NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES), [NET-HOSTS-CONNECT](#NET-HOSTS-CONNECT), [NET-HOSTS-DISCONNECT](#NET-HOSTS-DISCONNECT), [NET-HOSTS-LOCALHOST](#NET-HOSTS-LOCALHOST)

A container's /etc/hosts has lines that define the container's own hostname, besides localhost
and other common entries.

<a id="REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES**: A service's Hosts entries map their names and aliases in its containers

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* api/openapi.yaml: definition TaskSpec (ContainerSpec.Hosts)

*Refined by:* [NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES](#NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES) · *Violated by:* [NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED](#NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED), [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

ContainerSpec.Hosts lists hostname to IP address mappings to add to the hosts file of a
service's containers. Each entry has the form of a line of hosts(5): an IP address, a canonical
hostname, and optional aliases.

<a id="REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME**: An endpoint's ifname option names its interface in the container

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/28/#2800

*Refined by:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED) · *Violated by:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE](#NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE)

The endpoint option com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname sets the name of the container's
interface, for every built-in driver on Linux.

<a id="REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION**: Network inspect reports the network's configuration as created

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* api/openapi.yaml: definition Network (Created/Scope/Driver/EnableIPv6/IPAM/Internal/Attachable/Ingress/ConfigFrom/Labels); api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkInspect

*Refined by:* [NET-API-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION](#NET-API-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION), [SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED), [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES), [SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-MANAGER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-MANAGER), [SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-TASK-NODE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-TASK-NODE)

GET /networks/{id} reports a network's scope, when it was created, its IPAM configuration, the
name of the driver used to create it, and the EnableIPv6, Internal, Attachable, Ingress,
ConfigFrom and Labels that it was created with.

<a id="REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT**: An interface without a requested name is named eth<N>

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Images and scripts that name eth0 inside the container in ip or tc or iptables commands or in the configuration of keepalived or Zeek or in an application's --interface flag. The bridge driver documentation gives com.docker.network.container_iface_prefix the default eth (https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#options)

*Refined by:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT)

On Linux, the interface of an endpoint on a network of a built-in driver, without a requested
name and without com.docker.network.container_iface_prefix, is named eth<N>. The interface of a
container's only endpoint is named eth0.

<a id="REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS**: Containers cannot reach other networks through an internal network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#internal

*Refines:* [PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS](../principles.md#PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS) · *Refined by:* [BR-ISO-INTERNAL-NO-FORWARD](bridge-networking.md#BR-ISO-INTERNAL-NO-FORWARD), [NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS) · *Violated by:* [NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS)

docker network create --internal restricts external access to the network. A container cannot
reach other networks through an internal network.

<a id="REQ-NET-IPV6-ONLY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-IPV6-ONLY**: A network can be created without IPv4, as an IPv6-only network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#ipv6-only-bridge-networks

*Refined by:* [BR-OPT-IPV4-DISABLED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-IPV4-DISABLED) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED), [SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED-CLI](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V4-DISABLED-CLI](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V4-DISABLED-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY)

IPv4 address allocation can be disabled when a network is created (--ipv4=false, EnableIPv4
false), giving an IPv6-only network.

<a id="REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS**: A container's requested link-local addresses must be link-local

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#network; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/connect/; api/openapi.yaml: definition EndpointIPAMConfig (LinkLocalIPs); https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/29/#2991; https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53923

*Refined by:* [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID](#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID), [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-CLI](#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-CLI), [NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS](#NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS), [NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-CLI](#NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-CLI)

--link-local-ip on docker run, docker create and docker network connect, which sets LinkLocalIPs
in the endpoint's IPAMConfig, gives the container IPv4 or IPv6 link-local addresses on the
network. Container create and network connect refuse an address that is not in 169.254.0.0/16 or
fe80::/10, or that has a zone, before they change the container.

<a id="REQ-NET-LIST-FILTER-INVALID"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-LIST-FILTER-INVALID**: An invalid network list filter responds 400

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/53676: a report of a 500 for such a filter; https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53678: the merged fix that makes it respond 400

*Refined by:* [NET-API-FILTER-INVALID](#NET-API-FILTER-INVALID), [NET-API-FILTER-INVALID-CLI](#NET-API-FILTER-INVALID-CLI)

A GET /networks filter that is not well formed, such as a type value other than builtin or
custom, is a client error, and the request responds 400.

<a id="REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS**: GET /networks filters by dangling and type with the documented values

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkList; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/ls/#filter; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v140-api-changes; api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkList; https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/31551: the merged change whose commit message says that dangling leaves out the builtin networks

*Refined by:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-FALSE](#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-FALSE), [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-TRUE](#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-TRUE), [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BOTH](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BOTH), [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED), [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED-WINDOWS](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED-WINDOWS), [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-CUSTOM](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-CUSTOM), [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-VALUES](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-VALUES) · *Violated by:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED](#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED)

The network list accepts the filters dangling and type. dangling true or 1 lists the networks
that are not predefined and that no container uses; false or 0 lists the predefined networks and
the networks that containers use. type builtin lists the predefined networks and custom the
user-defined ones. Several values of type are combined with OR.

<a id="REQ-NET-LIVE-RESTORE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-LIVE-RESTORE**: With live-restore, containers keep running while the daemon is down

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/daemon/live-restore/

*Refined by:* [NET-RESTART-LIVE-RESTORE](#NET-RESTART-LIVE-RESTORE)

With live-restore enabled, containers remain running when the daemon terminates or restarts, so
that daemon crashes, outages and upgrades do not interrupt them.

<a id="REQ-NET-LOOKUP"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-LOOKUP**: A network is found by its ID, its name or a short ID

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkInspect; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/rm/#remove-multiple-networks: an example that removes a network by its short ID; api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkDelete; moby/moby daemon/network.go: code comment on FindNetwork that lists the order: full ID then full name then partial ID

*Refined by:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX), [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI), [NET-API-DELETE-NOT-FOUND](#NET-API-DELETE-NOT-FOUND), [NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX](#NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX), [NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI](#NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI), [NET-API-INSPECT-NOT-FOUND](#NET-API-INSPECT-NOT-FOUND), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS-CLI](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS-CLI) · *Violated by:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED), [NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX](#NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX), [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND)

Network requests take a network's full ID, its name or a prefix of its ID, such as a short ID. A
full ID is matched first, then a name, then a prefix, and the first of these that matches a
network decides. GET /networks/{id} and DELETE /networks/{id} respond 404 when no network
matches, and DELETE /networks/{id} responds 400 when the name or ID prefix matches more than one
network at that rank.

<a id="REQ-NET-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT**: A macvlan network's parent can be a VLAN sub-interface that Docker creates

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/macvlan/#8021q-trunk-bridge-mode

*Refined by:* [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-CREATED](#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-CREATED) · *Violated by:* [NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED)

A macvlan network's parent can be named <interface>.<VLAN ID>. Docker interprets the name as a
sub-interface of <interface> and creates the sub-interface automatically.

<a id="REQ-NET-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-INTERNAL"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-INTERNAL**: A macvlan network without a parent interface is internal

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* moby/moby daemon/libnetwork/drivers/macvlan/macvlan_network.go: code comment on a network without a parent interface and the debug log message that the driver writes when it creates the dummy parent ("Empty -o parent= flags limit communications to other containers inside of network")

*Refined by:* [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-ISOLATED](#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-ISOLATED), [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-SAME-NETWORK](#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-SAME-NETWORK)

A macvlan network created without a parent interface is internal: its containers communicate
only with other containers on the network, and reach no address outside it.

<a id="REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE**: Creating a network with an existing network's name is refused

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v144-api-changes; https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/35030

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME), [NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI](#NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI), [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT-CLI](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)

Network names must be unique. A create with a duplicate name fails at every API version, and the
refusal responds 409.

<a id="REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED**: Predefined networks cannot be created by name, removed or pruned

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkCreate; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkDelete; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/prune/; api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkCreate

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME), [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI), [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER), [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED), [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI), [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED)

Creating a network named after a predefined network is forbidden (403), and so is removing a
predefined network. On a Swarm manager, the names of the Swarm's predefined networks, bridge and
host on Linux, conflict with those networks instead (409). The default bridge network cannot be
removed, and bridge, host and none are never pruned.

<a id="REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED**: Network prune removes unused networks and names them

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/prune/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/#prune-networks; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkPrune

*Refined by:* [NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-NO-SWARM](#NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-NO-SWARM), [NET-API-PRUNE-SWARM-MESH-EGRESS](#NET-API-PRUNE-SWARM-MESH-EGRESS), [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED), [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED-CLI](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED-CLI) · *Violated by:* [NET-API-PRUNE-CONFIG-ONLY-KEPT](#NET-API-PRUNE-CONFIG-ONLY-KEPT), [NET-API-PRUNE-STOPPED-CTR-NETWORK](#NET-API-PRUNE-STOPPED-CTR-NETWORK)

docker network prune and POST /networks/prune remove the networks that no container references,
never the system networks, and report the names of the networks deleted.

<a id="REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES**: Network names that the container network mode claims are reserved

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/51973: the merged change that reserves these names

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME), [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER)

The network name container, and every name that starts with container:, are reserved, because
the container network mode claims these names. Creating a network with such a name is refused
with 403, on Linux and Windows alike.

<a id="REQ-NET-START-FAILED-AUTO-REMOVED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-START-FAILED-AUTO-REMOVED**: An auto-remove container is removed when its start fails

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/20848: the merged move of auto-remove into the daemon whose stated intent includes this case

*Refined by:* [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-AUTO-REMOVE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-AUTO-REMOVE), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-AUTO-REMOVE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-AUTO-REMOVE)

A container created with auto-remove (--rm) is removed when its start fails.

<a id="REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT**: A container whose start fails remains and can be started again

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Users and tools that read State.Error with docker inspect after a failed start and that start the same container again once they fix the cause (docker start retries/docker compose up run again)

*Refined by:* [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-START), [NET-API-START-FAILED-EXITED-KEPT](#NET-API-START-FAILED-EXITED-KEPT), [NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT](#NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT), [NET-API-START-FAILED-STARTED-AGAIN](#NET-API-START-FAILED-STARTED-AGAIN), [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-CREATED](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-CREATED), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-STAYS-CREATED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-STAYS-CREATED)

When a start request fails for a container without auto-remove, the container remains, and its
State.Status is still created or exited, as before the request. It can be inspected, and started
again.

<a id="REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS**: A container gets its requested static address on a user-defined network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#network; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/connect/#ip; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/29/#2913: a container can be created with a specific IP address on a network that was not configured with a subnet

*Refined by:* [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS), [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT), [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-RESTART](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-RESTART) · *Violated by:* [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED)

--ip and --ip6 on docker run or docker network connect choose the container's address on a
user-defined network, also on one created without a subnet; the address is reapplied when the
container restarts.

<a id="REQ-NET-NETWORK-CREATE-ERRORS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-NET-NETWORK-CREATE-ERRORS**: Network create refuses a bad parameter with an error response

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkCreate

*Refined by:* [BR-FW-IP6TABLES-MISSING-NETWORK](bridge-networking.md#BR-FW-IP6TABLES-MISSING-NETWORK), [BR-FW-NFT-IPV6-MISSING-NETWORK](bridge-networking.md#BR-FW-NFT-IPV6-MISSING-NETWORK), [BR-GWMODE-ISOLATED-NOT-INTERNAL](bridge-networking.md#BR-GWMODE-ISOLATED-NOT-INTERNAL), [BR-GWMODE-ISOLATED-NOT-INTERNAL-CLI](bridge-networking.md#BR-GWMODE-ISOLATED-NOT-INTERNAL-CLI), [BR-GWMODE-UNKNOWN](bridge-networking.md#BR-GWMODE-UNKNOWN), [BR-GWMODE-UNKNOWN-CLI](bridge-networking.md#BR-GWMODE-UNKNOWN-CLI), [BR-ISO-NO-BR-NETFILTER-NO-ICC](bridge-networking.md#BR-ISO-NO-BR-NETFILTER-NO-ICC), [BR-NOV6-V6-NETWORK-REFUSED](bridge-networking.md#BR-NOV6-V6-NETWORK-REFUSED), [BR-OPT-MTU-INVALID](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-MTU-INVALID), [BR-OPT-MTU-INVALID-CLI](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-MTU-INVALID-CLI), [BR-OPT-MTU-REFUSED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-MTU-REFUSED), [BR-OPT-MTU-REFUSED-CLI](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-MTU-REFUSED-CLI), [IPVL-NETIF-MODE-FLAG-INVALID](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-MODE-FLAG-INVALID), [IPVL-NETIF-PARENT-INVALID](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-PARENT-INVALID), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING), [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-WRONG-KIND](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-WRONG-KIND) · *Violated by:* [BR-GWMODE-HTTP500-REFUSED](bridge-networking.md#BR-GWMODE-HTTP500-REFUSED), [BR-OPT-HTTP500-REFUSED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-HTTP500-REFUSED), [BR-OPT-MTU-MODULO](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-MTU-MODULO)

POST /networks/create documents status 400 for a bad parameter and 500 for a server error; a
refused request does not create the network.

<a id="network-common-rationales"></a>

## Rationales

<a id="RAT-NET-INGRESS-SBOX-ON-GWBRIDGE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-INGRESS-SBOX-ON-GWBRIDGE**: The ingress sandbox's endpoint on docker_gwbridge shows a node's part of the routing mesh

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-GWBRIDGE-INGRESS-SBOX](#NET-API-GWBRIDGE-INGRESS-SBOX), [NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-SWARM](#NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-SWARM)

[*NET-API-GWBRIDGE-INGRESS-SBOX*](#NET-API-GWBRIDGE-INGRESS-SBOX) notices a change to when a node gives its ingress sandbox
an endpoint on `docker_gwbridge`, or to how `GET /networks/docker_gwbridge`
reports it. Operators debugging the routing mesh look for `ingress-sbox` there to tell whether
a node has set up its part of the mesh, and the endpoint is what keeps
`docker_gwbridge` from `POST /networks/prune`
([*NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-SWARM*](#NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-SWARM)). Renaming the endpoint, moving it, or setting it up later
than the init or join would mislead that debugging and change what a prune leaves, so such a
change should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS**: Driver properties decide a container's interfaces and its MAC requests

*Rationale of:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

Expectations in several specs are scoped by a property of the network's driver, such as "a
driver that adds an interface to the container" or "a driver that accepts an endpoint MAC
address", and do not list the drivers. [*NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE*](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE) and
[*NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC*](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC) say which built-in drivers have each property. A driver that
started or stopped adding an interface would add or remove an interface in every container on
its networks, so the operator's tooling and debugging inside the container would see a different
set of interfaces. A driver that started or stopped accepting an endpoint MAC address would
change which requests that set `MacAddress` for an endpoint on its networks succeed.
Either change should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-NET-FILTER-NO-MATCH-NOT-REFUSED"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-FILTER-NO-MATCH-NOT-REFUSED**: A filter that matches nothing is an empty result, not a refusal

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-FILTER-NO-MATCH](#NET-API-FILTER-NO-MATCH)

[*NET-API-FILTER-INVALID*](#NET-API-FILTER-INVALID) refuses a filter that is not well formed. A well-formed filter
value that matches no network gives an empty list instead, as the Engine API's other list
requests do for a filter that matches nothing. A change that refused such a value would make an
empty selection look like a malformed request, and set the network list apart from its sibling
requests. It should be made by decision.

<a id="RAT-NET-NAME-DEFAULT-REFUSED"></a>

**Rationale RAT-NET-NAME-DEFAULT-REFUSED**: A network named default could not be told from the default network mode

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-CREATE-DEFAULT-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-DEFAULT-NAME)

In a container's `HostConfig.NetworkMode`, `default` selects the daemon's default
network, so a network with that name could not be named there. No source reserves the name, as
[*REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES*](#REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES) does for `container`. A change that lets such a network be
created should be made together with a decision about what `default` then selects.

<a id="network-common-host-requirements"></a>

## Host requirements

The kernel facilities and the host configuration are requirements of each Linux node. The
conventions for this section are in [README.md](README.md#readme-host-requirements). The specs of the
drivers list what each driver needs, in the host requirements of [bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md#bridge-networking-host-requirements), [swarm-networking.md](swarm-networking.md#swarm-networking-host-requirements) and [ipvlan-networking.md](ipvlan-networking.md#ipvlan-networking-host-requirements).

[SWARM-SD-TASK-NAME-REPLICATED](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-TASK-NAME-REPLICATED), [SWARM-SD-TASK-STOPPED](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-TASK-STOPPED), [SWARM-SD-TASKS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-TASKS), [SWARM-SD-TASKS-ALIAS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-TASKS-ALIAS), [SWARM-SD-VIP](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-VIP), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-REPLICAS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-REPLICAS), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-TASKS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-VIP-NO-TASKS), [SWARM-SD-VIP-NONE-HEALTHY](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-VIP-NONE-HEALTHY), [SWARM-SD-VIP-UNREACHABLE](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-VIP-UNREACHABLE), [SWARM-WIRE-ADDRESS-ASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-ADDRESS-ASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-WIRE-MIXED-VERSIONS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-MIXED-VERSIONS), [SWARM-WIRE-NO-VXLAN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-NO-VXLAN), [SWARM-WIRE-NO-VXLAN-MSG](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-NO-VXLAN-MSG), [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD), [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-UDP-PORT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-UDP-PORT), [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-VXLAN-VNI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-VXLAN-VNI), [SWARM-WIREENC-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIREENC-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD), [SWARM-WIREENC-UDP-PORT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIREENC-UDP-PORT), [SWARM-WIREENC-VXLAN-VNI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIREENC-VXLAN-VNI)

*Facility:* The host's firewall passes the traffic that an expectation involves, to and from the
node, its containers and its published ports. The rules and the firewalld configuration that the
daemon programs are not part of the host's firewall.

*Needed when:* Always. In an expectation whose state or statement names firewalld, the host's
firewall is firewalld, running with the configuration that the node's operating system installs,
so that firewalld's default zone applies to the node's interfaces. Its only additions open the
traffic that a host configuration requirement of the expectation's spec names, such as the Swarm
ports ([*SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS*](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS)), with configuration that a firewalld reload
keeps. Where the expectation's spec has no such requirement, as [bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md) and [container-dns.md](container-dns.md) do not, firewalld passes the
expectation's traffic only where its installed configuration or the configuration that the
daemon programs passes it. An expectation that names neither firewalld nor its absence holds
whether or not firewalld runs. On a node where firewalld runs, such an expectation holds with
the configuration that the node's baseline gives firewalld. For a daemon installed from a
package, that is the configuration that the operating system installs and the setup that the
product's installation documentation prescribes, so traffic that firewalld drops there fails the
expectation unless a defect that narrows it states the case. For any other daemon, it is a
configuration that passes the expectation's traffic.

<a id="network-common-network-api"></a>

## Network API

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME**: Creating a network with an existing network's name responds 409

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE](#REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI](#NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* An existing network that is not Swarm-scoped and not predefined

`POST /networks/create` with the network's name responds 409. `GET /networks`
then lists only one network with that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME-CLI**: docker network create with an existing network's name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE](#REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-DUPLICATE-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* An existing network that is not Swarm-scoped and not predefined

`docker network create` with the network's name exits non-zero and prints the daemon's
error. `docker network ls` then lists only one network with that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME**: Outside a manager, a predefined or reserved network name responds 403

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED](#REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED), [REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES](#REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A node that is not a Swarm manager

`POST /networks/create` with the name of a predefined network or `container` responds
403. `POST /networks/create` with a name that starts with `container:` also responds
403. `GET /networks` then does not list a new network with that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-DEFAULT-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CREATE-DEFAULT-NAME**: A network named default is refused with 403

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* A network named default could not be told from the default network mode ([RAT-NET-NAME-DEFAULT-REFUSED](#RAT-NET-NAME-DEFAULT-REFUSED))

`POST /networks/create` with the name `default` responds 403, on a node that
is not in a Swarm and on a Swarm node. `GET /networks` then does not list a network
with that name.

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-CLI**: docker network create with a predefined network's name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED](#REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME](#NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker network create` with the name of a predefined network exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED**: Deleting a predefined network responds 403

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED](#REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND)

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for a predefined network responds 403. `GET /networks`
then still lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI**: docker network rm of a predefined network fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED](#REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND)

`docker network rm` for a predefined network exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error.
`docker network ls` then still lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE**: Deleting a network with a running container is refused

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-DELETE-IN-USE](#REQ-NET-DELETE-IN-USE) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, with a running container attached to it

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds with a 4xx status. `GET
/networks` then still lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-HTTP403**: Deleting a network with a running container responds 403

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, with a running container attached to it

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 403. `GET /networks` then still

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI**: docker network rm of a network with a running container fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DELETE-IN-USE](#REQ-NET-DELETE-IN-USE) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE](#NET-API-DELETE-IN-USE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)
