<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED**: Connecting a running container to a network it is attached to fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-CONNECT-ONCE](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-ONCE) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-HTTP403](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-HTTP403), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-HTTP409](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-HTTP409) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-CLI](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container attached to a network

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds with a 4xx
status, also when its endpoint settings request another address in `IPAMConfig`. The
container's addresses on that network do not change.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-HTTP403**: A repeat connect to a network that is not Swarm-scoped responds 403

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container attached to a network that is not Swarm-scoped

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds 403.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-CLI**: docker network connect to a network already attached fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CONNECT-ONCE](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-ONCE) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container attached to a network

`docker network connect` naming that network and the container exits non-zero and prints
the daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED**: A repeat connect of a created or stopped container responds 200

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CONNECT-REPEAT-STOPPED](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-REPEAT-STOPPED) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-CLI](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-SETTINGS](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-SETTINGS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container whose `NetworkSettings.Networks` lists a
network that is not Swarm-scoped

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, without endpoint
settings or with endpoint settings that the daemon accepts for that network, responds 200.
`NetworkSettings.Networks` of the container then still lists the network.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-CLI**: A repeat docker network connect of a created or stopped container succeeds

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CONNECT-REPEAT-STOPPED](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-REPEAT-STOPPED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container whose `NetworkSettings.Networks` lists a
network that is not Swarm-scoped

`docker network connect` naming that network and the container, without options or with
options that the daemon accepts for that network, exits zero. `docker inspect` for the
container then still lists the network in `NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-SETTINGS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED-SETTINGS**: A repeat connect of a stopped container drops the new endpoint settings

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED](#NET-API-CONNECT-ALREADY-ATTACHED-STOPPED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container whose `NetworkSettings.Networks` lists a
network that is not Swarm-scoped

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with endpoint settings
that the daemon accepts for that network and that differ from the stored ones, such as other
aliases, responds 200. The container's endpoint settings for the network do not change.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED**: A created or stopped container connects to a network

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-CLI](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container attached to a bridge network, and a user-defined
bridge network that it is not attached to

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds 200.
`GET /containers/{id}/json` then lists the network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`. After `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the
container responds 204, the container has an interface on the network.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-CLI**: docker network connect of a created or stopped container succeeds

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container attached to a bridge network, and a user-defined
bridge network that it is not attached to

`docker network connect` naming that network and the container exits zero. `docker
inspect` for the container then lists the network in `NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX**: A created or stopped container's connect by a shared ID prefix responds 200

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED), [NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX) · *Violates:* [PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE](../principles.md#PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, two or more networks whose IDs start with a prefix
that is not a network name, and a created or stopped container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with that prefix as `{id}`, responds
200. `GET /containers/{id}/json` for the container then lists the prefix in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS**: A connect to a missing network gives no warning, and the start responds 404

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER](#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER](#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, with a created or stopped container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an `{id}` that is not the name
or an ID prefix of any network, responds 200 without a warning. `POST
/containers/{id}/start` for the container then responds 404 while no network has that name, with
a message that contains `network <name> not found`.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER**: A container connected to a missing network uses it once it is created

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pins:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS](#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS](#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-START-FAILS), [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS](#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an `{id}` that is not the name
or an ID prefix of any network, responds 200. A network with that name that is not config-only
is then created. `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container then responds 204, and
the container has an address on that network.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET**: A static address outside the network's subnets is refused

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST), [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-HTTP400](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-HTTP400) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-CLI](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped and that, on a Windows node, was created with a
subnet in `IPAM.Config`, and a container that is not attached to it

`POST /containers/create` with a static address in `IPAMConfig` that is
outside every subnet of that network responds with a 4xx status, and does not create a
container. `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with that
address, responds with a 4xx status, and does not attach the container.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-HTTP400**: A static address outside the network's subnets responds 400

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped and that, on a Windows node, was created with a
subnet in `IPAM.Config`, and a container that is not attached to it

`POST /containers/create` with a static address in `IPAMConfig` that is
outside every subnet of that network responds 400, and does not create a container.
`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with that address,
responds 400, and does not attach the container.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: A static address on the default bridge is refused

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST), [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-HTTP400](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-HTTP400) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CLI](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A create naming the default bridge by its ID accepts a static address ([NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container that is not attached to the network `bridge`

`POST /containers/create` with a static address in `IPAMConfig` for the
network `bridge` responds with a 4xx status, and does not create a container.
`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to the network `bridge`, for the container, with
a static address in `IPAMConfig`, responds with a 4xx status, and does not attach the
container.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-HTTP400**: A static address on the default bridge responds 400

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A create naming the default bridge by its ID accepts a static address ([NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container that is not attached to the network `bridge`

`POST /containers/create` with a static address in `IPAMConfig` for the
network `bridge` responds 400, and does not create a container. `POST
/networks/{id}/connect` to the network `bridge`, for the container, with a static
address in `IPAMConfig`, responds 400, and does not attach the container.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ID**: A create naming the default bridge by its ID accepts a static address

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE), [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-HTTP400](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-HTTP400) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST)

`POST /containers/create` whose `NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig` names the
network `bridge` by its ID, or by a prefix of its ID, with a static address in
`IPAMConfig` that a subnet of the network contains, responds 201 and creates the
container. `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container then responds with a 4xx
status and does not start it.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CLI**: docker run and docker network connect with --ip on the default bridge fail

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-DEFAULT-BRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run` and `docker network connect` with `--ip` for the network
`bridge` exit non-zero and print the daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET-CLI**: docker run and docker network connect with a refused --ip fail

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET](#NET-API-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-SUBNET) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run` and `docker network connect` with `--ip` outside every subnet
of a network that is not Swarm-scoped exit non-zero and print the daemon's error. On Windows
nodes, they do so for a network that was created with a subnet.

<a id="NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID**: A LinkLocalIPs entry that is not link-local or has a zone is refused

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-HTTP400](#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-HTTP400) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-CLI](#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, and a container that is not attached to it

`POST /containers/create` with an address that is not in `169.254.0.0/16` or
`fe80::/10`, or an address with a zone, such as `fe80::1%eth0`, in
`IPAMConfig.LinkLocalIPs` for that network responds with a 4xx status, and does not
create a container. `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container,
with such an address, responds with a 4xx status, and does not attach the container.

<a id="NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-HTTP400**: An invalid LinkLocalIPs entry responds 400 and says the IP is invalid

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID](#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, and a container that is not attached to it

`POST /containers/create` with an address that is not in `169.254.0.0/16` or
`fe80::/10`, or an address with a zone, such as `fe80::1%eth0`, in
`IPAMConfig.LinkLocalIPs` for that network responds 400, with a message that contains
`invalid link-local IP address`. So does `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to
that network, for the container, with such an address.

<a id="NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID-CLI**: A --link-local-ip that is not link-local fails docker run and connect

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID](#NET-API-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run` and `docker network connect` with `--link-local-ip` set to an
address that is not in `169.254.0.0/16` or `fe80::/10`, for a network that is not
Swarm-scoped, exit non-zero and print the daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED**: At API version 1.43 or earlier, create on several networks is refused

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS](#REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED-HTTP400](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED-HTTP400) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

At API version 1.43 or earlier, `POST /containers/create` with more than one network in
`NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig` responds with a 4xx status, and does not create a
container.

<a id="NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED-HTTP400**: At API version 1.43 or earlier, create on several networks responds 400

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-REFUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

At API version 1.43 or earlier, `POST /containers/create` with more than one network in
`NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig` responds 400, and does not create a container.

<a id="NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS**: At API version 1.44 or later, a container is created on several networks

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS](#REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-CLI](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Two networks that are not Swarm-scoped, not predefined and not config-only

At API version 1.44 or later, `POST /containers/create` with both networks in
`NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig` responds 201. `GET /containers/{id}/json`
then lists both networks in `NetworkSettings.Networks`. After `POST
/containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 204, `GET /containers/{id}/json`
reports a non-empty `EndpointID` for each of the two networks.

<a id="NET-API-CTR-CREATE-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CTR-CREATE-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: A container created without a network is attached to the default bridge

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ATTACHMENT](#REQ-NET-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-ATTACHMENT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose daemon has the default bridge enabled

`POST /containers/create` without `HostConfig.NetworkMode` and without
`NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig` responds 201. `GET /containers/{id}/json`
then reports the default bridge network, `bridge`, and no other network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS-CLI**: docker run with two --network flags attaches the container to both

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS](#REQ-NET-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-MULTIPLE-NETWORKS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Two networks that are not Swarm-scoped, not predefined and not config-only

`docker run -d` with a `--network` flag for each of the two networks exits zero.
`docker inspect` for the container then lists both networks in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED**: Disconnecting a container from a network it is not attached to fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-CLI](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED)

*Applies to:* A container, and a network that it is not attached to

`POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container from that network responds with a 4xx
or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500**: Disconnecting from a network the container is not on responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED) · *Pins:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED)

*Applies to:* A container, and a network that it is not attached to

`POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container from that network responds 500, with
a message that contains `is not connected to`.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-CLI**: docker network disconnect from a network not attached fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container, and a network that it is not attached to

`docker network disconnect` naming that network and the container exits non-zero and prints
the daemon's error.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING**: A running container disconnects from a network and keeps running

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-CLI](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a network other than `host`, from
its start or from a later connect

`POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container responds 200. `GET
/containers/{id}/json` then does not list the network in `NetworkSettings.Networks`,
and the container still runs.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-IFACE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-IFACE**: A disconnected container no longer has its interface on the network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A disconnect leaves an interface whose name the kernel numbered ([NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT))

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a network other than `host`, from
its start or from a later connect

After `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container responds 200, the container
does not have its interface on that network.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-DISCONNECT-IFACE-LEFT**: A disconnect leaves an interface whose name the kernel numbered

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-IFACE](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-IFACE), [SWARM-CTR-DISCONNECT](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-DISCONNECT) · *Violates:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS), [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT)

For an endpoint whose requested interface name contains `%d`, `POST
/networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container responds 200, but the interface stays in the
container. The interface stays up and keeps its address.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING-CLI**: docker network disconnect of a running container succeeds

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-RUNNING) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a network other than `host`, from
its start or from a later connect

`docker network disconnect` for the container exits zero. `docker inspect` for the
container then does not list the network in `NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED**: A created or stopped container disconnects from a listed network

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED-CLI](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container whose `NetworkSettings.Networks` lists a
network

`POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container from that network responds 200.
`GET /containers/{id}/json` then does not list the network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED-CLI**: docker network disconnect of a created or stopped container succeeds

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-DISCONNECT](#REQ-NET-DISCONNECT) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-STOPPED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container whose `NetworkSettings.Networks` lists a
network

`docker network disconnect` naming that network and the container exits zero. `docker
inspect` for the container then does not list the network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

<a id="NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX**: A network is found by its full ID, its name or a unique ID prefix

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](#REQ-NET-LOOKUP) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI](#NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* On a manager, a name finds the Swarm-scoped network whose ID it prefixes ([NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX](#NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX)) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)

`GET /networks/{id}` responds 200 with the network when `{id}` is the network's full
ID, or its name when no other network has that name. It does the same when `{id}` is a prefix
of the network's ID that the ID of no other network starts with, and that is not the name of
another network.

<a id="NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI**: docker network inspect finds a network by ID, name or unique prefix

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](#REQ-NET-LOOKUP) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX](#NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* On a manager, a name finds the Swarm-scoped network whose ID it prefixes ([NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX](#NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX)) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)

`docker network inspect` prints the network when it is given the network's full ID, or its
name when no other network has that name. It does the same when it is given a prefix of the
network's ID that the ID of no other network starts with, and that is not the name of another
network.

<a id="NET-API-INSPECT-NOT-FOUND"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-INSPECT-NOT-FOUND**: Inspecting a network that matches no ID, name or prefix responds 404

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](#REQ-NET-LOOKUP) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks/{id}` responds 404 when `{id}` is not the full ID, the name or a prefix
of the ID of any network.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-NOT-FOUND"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-NOT-FOUND**: Deleting a network that matches no ID, name or prefix responds 404

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](#REQ-NET-LOOKUP) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`DELETE /networks/{id}` responds 404 when `{id}` is not the full ID, the name or a
prefix of the ID of any network.

<a id="NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX**: Inspecting by an ID prefix that several networks share fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE](../principles.md#PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-HTTP400](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-HTTP400) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A prefix shared with the Swarm's bridge or host returns the other network ([NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED)), On a manager, an ID prefix shared with one Swarm-scoped network returns it ([NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-SCOPED](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-SCOPED)) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](#NET-API-CONNECT-STOPPED-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX)

*Applies to:* Two or more networks whose IDs start with a prefix that is not a network name

`GET /networks/{id}` with that prefix as `{id}` responds with a 4xx status.

<a id="NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-HTTP400**: An ID prefix that several networks share responds 400

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A prefix shared with the Swarm's bridge or host returns the other network ([NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED)), On a manager, an ID prefix shared with one Swarm-scoped network returns it ([NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-SCOPED](#NET-API-INSPECT-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-SCOPED))

*Applies to:* Two or more networks whose IDs start with a prefix that is not a network name

`GET /networks/{id}` with that prefix as `{id}` responds 400, with a message that
contains `is ambiguous`.

<a id="NET-API-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION**: GET /networks/{id} reports Scope local and the network's create fields

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION](#REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network of a built-in node-local driver that is not Swarm-scoped, created
without `ConfigFrom`

`GET /networks/{id}` for the network reports `Scope` as `local`, and
reports `Created`. It also reports the `Driver`, `Internal`,
`Attachable`, `EnableIPv6` and `Labels` given at create, and
in `IPAM.Config` the subnets given at create.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX**: Deleting by an ID prefix that several networks share responds 400

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE](../principles.md#PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](#REQ-NET-LOOKUP) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED)

*Applies to:* Two or more networks that are not Swarm-scoped, whose IDs start with a prefix that
is not a network name

`DELETE /networks/{id}` with that prefix as `{id}` responds 400. `GET
/networks` then still lists each of the networks.

<a id="NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-CLI**: docker network rm by an ID prefix that several networks share fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE](../principles.md#PRIN-AMBIGUITY-NOT-DESTRUCTIVE), [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](#REQ-NET-LOOKUP) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-DELETE-AMBIGUOUS-PREFIX-SWARM-PREDEFINED)

*Applies to:* Two or more networks that are not Swarm-scoped, whose IDs start with a prefix that
is not a network name

`docker network rm` with that prefix exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error.
`docker network ls` then still lists each of the networks.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-CUSTOM"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-CUSTOM**: The filter type=custom lists the networks that type=builtin does not

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks` with the filter `type=custom` lists the networks, other than
the Swarm's predefined networks, that the filter `type=builtin` does not list. It
does not list a network that the filter `type=builtin` lists.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED**: type=builtin lists host and none, and bridge while it exists

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks` with the filter `type=builtin` lists `host` and
`none`. It also lists `bridge` while the default bridge network exists.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN**: The filter type=builtin lists no network but host, none and bridge

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks` with the filter `type=builtin` lists `host` and
`none`, `bridge` while the default bridge network exists, and no other network.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED-WINDOWS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED-WINDOWS**: On Windows, type=builtin lists none, and nat while it exists

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-WINDOWS](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-WINDOWS)

`GET /networks` with the filter `type=builtin` lists `none`. It also lists
`nat` while a network named `nat` exists.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-WINDOWS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-WINDOWS**: On Windows, the filter type=builtin lists no network but none and nat

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED-WINDOWS](#NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BUILTIN-PREDEFINED-WINDOWS)

`GET /networks` with the filter `type=builtin` lists `none`, `nat`
while a network named `nat` exists, and no other network.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-INVALID"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-INVALID**: An unknown filter term or a bad type or dangling value responds 400

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTER-INVALID](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTER-INVALID) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-FILTER-INVALID-CLI](#NET-API-FILTER-INVALID-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks` with a filter term that it does not support responds 400. It also
responds 400 for a value of the `type` or `dangling` term that the term
does not accept, and for more than one value for `dangling`.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-NO-MATCH"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-FILTER-NO-MATCH**: A well-formed filter that matches no network lists none

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* A filter that matches nothing is an empty result, not a refusal ([RAT-NET-FILTER-NO-MATCH-NOT-REFUSED](#RAT-NET-FILTER-NO-MATCH-NOT-REFUSED))

`GET /networks` with a value of a supported filter term other than `type` and
`dangling` that matches no network responds 200 and lists no network.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-INVALID-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-INVALID-CLI**: docker network ls with an unsupported filter term or value fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTER-INVALID](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTER-INVALID) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-FILTER-INVALID](#NET-API-FILTER-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker network ls --filter` exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error for a filter term
that the daemon does not support. It does the same for a value of the `type` or
`dangling` term that the term does not accept.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-VALUES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-VALUES**: The type and dangling filter terms each accept a fixed set of values

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks` with `type=builtin` or `type=custom` responds 200.
With `dangling` set to one of `true`, `1`, `false` or `0`, it responds 200.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BOTH"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-TYPE-BOTH**: With both type values, the filter lists every network

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`GET /networks` with both `type=builtin` and `type=custom` lists
every network other than the Swarm's predefined networks.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-TRUE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-TRUE**: The filter dangling=true lists a network with no running container

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED](#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped and not predefined, with no running container
attached to it, other than `docker_gwbridge` on a Linux node in a Swarm that has an
ingress network created with `Ingress` set

`GET /networks` with the filter `dangling=true` lists the network, and with
the filter `dangling=false` does not list it.

<a id="NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-FALSE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-FALSE**: The filter dangling=false lists a predefined or in-use network

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS](#REQ-NET-LIST-FILTERS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED](#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, and that is predefined or has a running
container attached to it

`GET /networks` with the filter `dangling=false` lists the network, and with
the filter `dangling=true` does not list it.

<a id="NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED**: Network prune deletes unused networks and lists their names

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED](#REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED), [REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED](#REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED-CLI](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* Network prune deletes a network that only stopped containers list ([NET-API-PRUNE-STOPPED-CTR-NETWORK](#NET-API-PRUNE-STOPPED-CTR-NETWORK)) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-PRUNE-CONFIG-ONLY-KEPT](#NET-API-PRUNE-CONFIG-ONLY-KEPT)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm

`POST /networks/prune` responds 200. It deletes each network that is not Swarm-scoped,
not predefined, not config-only and not adopted from the host, and that no container lists in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`. It does not delete a predefined network, or a network
that a container lists in `NetworkSettings.Networks`. On Windows nodes, it does not
delete a network that the daemon adopted from the host: one with
`com.docker.network.windowsshim.hnsowned` in its `Options`, or one named
`Default Switch` or `WSL (Hyper-V firewall)`. `NetworksDeleted` in the response
lists the names of the networks that it deletes.

<a id="NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED-CLI**: docker network prune --force deletes unused networks and names them

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED](#REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm

`docker network prune --force` exits zero, and prints the names of the networks that it
deletes. `docker network ls` then does not list those networks.

<a id="NET-API-PRUNE-STOPPED-CTR-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-PRUNE-STOPPED-CTR-NETWORK**: Network prune deletes a network that only stopped containers list

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED](#REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, and a network that is not Swarm-scoped, not
predefined and not config-only, that a created or stopped container lists in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`, and that no running container is attached to

`POST /networks/prune` deletes the network, and `NetworksDeleted` lists its
name. `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container then responds 404 while no network
has that name.

<a id="NET-API-PRUNE-CONFIG-ONLY-KEPT"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-PRUNE-CONFIG-ONLY-KEPT**: Network prune keeps a config-only network that nothing uses

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED](#NET-API-PRUNE-UNUSED) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED](#REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, and a config-only network that no container lists
in `NetworkSettings.Networks` and that no network's `ConfigFrom` names

`POST /networks/prune` responds 200, and does not delete the network.
`NetworksDeleted` does not list its name.

<a id="NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-NO-SWARM"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-PRUNE-GWBRIDGE-NO-SWARM**: Outside a Swarm, network prune deletes an unused docker_gwbridge

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED](#REQ-NET-PRUNE-UNUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, and a `docker_gwbridge` network that no
container lists in `NetworkSettings.Networks`

`POST /networks/prune` deletes `docker_gwbridge`. This includes a
`docker_gwbridge` that an operator creates before the node joins a Swarm, to configure
the gateway network.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CREATE**: A network created with ConfigOnly reports ConfigOnly true

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CONFIG-ONLY](#REQ-NET-CONFIG-ONLY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`POST /networks/create` with `ConfigOnly` true, without
`ConfigFrom` and `Scope`, and with `Ingress`,
`Internal` and `Attachable` false or unset, responds 201 when its
`Driver` is not `overlay` or the node is a manager. `GET
/networks/{id}` then reports `ConfigOnly` true.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-IPAM"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-IPAM**: A ConfigFrom network reports the config-only network's IPAM

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM](#REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network that is not Swarm-scoped, created with `ConfigFrom` naming a
config-only network

`GET /networks/{id}` for the network reports the config-only network's `IPAM`
configuration.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-ADDRESSES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-ADDRESSES**: A ConfigFrom network's containers get addresses in the config subnets

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM](#REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network created with `ConfigFrom` naming a config-only network

The interface of a running container on the network has an address in a subnet of the
config-only network's `IPAM` configuration, for each IP version that the config-only
network enables and that its configuration has a subnet for.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING**: Creating a network with a missing ConfigFrom network fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM](#REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM), [REQ-NET-NETWORK-CREATE-ERRORS](#REQ-NET-NETWORK-CREATE-ERRORS) · *Exact form:* [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-HTTP404](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-HTTP404) · *CLI form:* [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CLI](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`POST /networks/create` with `ConfigFrom` naming a network that does not
exist responds with a 4xx status. `GET /networks` then does not list a network
with the request's `Name`.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-HTTP404"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-HTTP404**: A missing ConfigFrom network responds 404

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING](#NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`POST /networks/create` with `ConfigFrom` naming a network that does not
exist responds 404, with a message that contains `configuration network "<name>" does
not exist`.

<a id="NET-API-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CLI"></a>

*Exact form of:* [NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING](#NET-API-CONFIG-ONLY-CONNECT-RUNNING) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a config-only network

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, responds 403, with a
message that contains `cannot create endpoint on configuration-only network`.

`docker network connect` naming that network and the container exits non-zero and prints

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED**: A failed connect leaves the network out of the container's settings

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS), [REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](#NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network that it is not attached to

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, fails, whatever
the reason, `GET /containers/{id}/json` does not list the network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`, and `GET /networks/{id}` does not list the
container. On Linux nodes, this includes a connect, at API version 1.54 or later, to an
`ipvlan` network with `MacAddress` set in the endpoint settings, which fails
when the daemon creates the endpoint.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-IFACE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-IFACE**: A failed connect adds no interface to the container

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A connect refused at the interface name leaves the interface in the container ([NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](#NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT))

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network that it is not attached to

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, fails, whatever
the reason, the container has the same interfaces as before the request. On Linux nodes, this
includes a connect whose `com.docker.network.endpoint.sysctls` sets a setting of the new
interface that the kernel does not have, which fails after the daemon has added the interface to
the container.

<a id="NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT**: A connect refused at the interface name leaves the interface in the container

*Observed from:* ctr, node · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-IFACE](#NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-IFACE) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED](#NET-API-CONNECT-FAILED-NOT-LISTED), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT) · *Violates:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS)

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running container fails, with a
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that the OS refuses or that names `lo` or
one of the container's interfaces, the interface stays in the container under the name that the
driver generated for it. The interface is down and does not have addresses. It stays until the
container's network namespace is destroyed. For a bridge network, the interface is a
`veth`, and its peer stays attached to the network's bridge on the node until then.

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-CTR-CREATE-HOST-PORT-HELD**: A container whose host port another one holds is created without a warning

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT](#NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD)

*Applies to:* A running container that publishes a host port

`POST /containers/create` for a container on a bridge network that publishes the same
host port responds 201 without a warning about the host port.

<a id="NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-START-FAILED-NETWORKS-KEPT**: A start that fails at network setup keeps the container's networks

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE), [REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT](#REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-CTR-CREATE-HOST-PORT-HELD](#NET-API-CTR-CREATE-HOST-PORT-HELD)

*Applies to:* A running container that publishes a host port, and a created container without
`HostConfig.AutoRemove` on a bridge network that publishes the same host port

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the created container responds with a 4xx or 5xx
status. `GET /containers/{id}/json` then reports `State.Status` as
`created`, and lists in `NetworkSettings.Networks` each network that it listed
before the start. A second `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container also
responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-API-START-FAILED-EXITED-KEPT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-START-FAILED-EXITED-KEPT**: A failed start leaves an exited container exited

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT](#REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that publishes a host port, and an exited container without
`HostConfig.AutoRemove` on a bridge network that publishes the same host port

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the exited container responds with a 4xx or 5xx
status. `GET /containers/{id}/json` then reports `State.Status` as
`exited`.

<a id="NET-API-START-FAILED-STARTED-AGAIN"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-START-FAILED-STARTED-AGAIN**: A container whose start failed starts once the cause is gone

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT](#REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A created container without `HostConfig.AutoRemove` on a bridge network
that publishes a host port, whose start failed while a running container published the same host

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the created container responds 204. `GET
/containers/{id}/json` then reports `State.Status` as `running`.

<a id="NET-API-START-FAILED-ENDPOINT-NOT-LISTED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-START-FAILED-ENDPOINT-NOT-LISTED**: After a failed start, the container list reports no endpoint for it

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS), [REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE](#REQ-NET-CONNECT-FAILED-NO-TRACE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that publishes a host port, and a created container without
`HostConfig.AutoRemove` on a bridge network that publishes the same host port

After `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the created container fails, `GET
/containers/json` with `all` set reports an empty `EndpointID` and an
empty `IPAddress` for each of the container's networks.

<a id="network-common-network-api-in-a-swarm"></a>

### In a Swarm

<a id="NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-API-CREATE-PREDEFINED-NAME-MANAGER**: On a manager, the names bridge and host respond 409, the rest 403

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE](#REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE), [REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED](#REQ-NET-PREDEFINED-RESERVED), [REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES](#REQ-NET-RESERVED-NAMES) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Linux manager

`POST /networks/create` with the name `bridge` or `host` responds 409.
It responds 403 when the name is `none` or `container`, or starts with
`container:`. This holds for the default driver and for `overlay`.

<a id="NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS**: In a Swarm, a connect to a missing network gives no warning, and start gets 500

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pins:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER](#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-CREATED-LATER) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS)

*Applies to:* A node in a Swarm, and a created or stopped container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an `{id}` that is not the name
or an ID prefix of any network, responds 200 without a warning. `POST
/containers/{id}/start` for the container then responds 500, with a message that contains
`network <name> not found`. `<name>` is the `{id}` that the connect gave.

<a id="NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-API-NAME-SWARM-ID-PREFIX**: On a manager, a name finds the Swarm-scoped network whose ID it prefixes

<a id="network-common-endpoint-interfaces"></a>

## Endpoint interfaces

The expectations in this section about an endpoint hold for an endpoint of any network driver that
adds an interface to the container ([Driver properties](#network-common-driver-properties)). An endpoint requests
an interface name when its `com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` is set to that name. The
section also holds the macvlan driver's expectations about its `parent` interface.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED**: An endpoint's interface has the name that it requests

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME](#REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A requested name with %d is accepted, and the kernel numbers it ([NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE](#NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE)) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER](#NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER), [NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED](#NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED)

*Applies to:* An endpoint that requests an interface name, on a container none of whose
endpoints that request no name is on a network whose interface prefix (`eth`, or the value of
its `com.docker.network.container_iface_prefix`), followed by a number, is that name

The interface has that name.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-NAME-COLLISION-ORDER**: Whether a start succeeds depends on the order of attaching endpoints

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-REPEATABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-REPEATABLE)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes

At API version 1.44 or later, `POST /containers/create` for a container with two
endpoints on networks of drivers that add an interface, one that requests the interface name
`eth0` and one that requests no name, responds 201. Repeated
`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container, each after the container stops, give
both outcomes: some respond 204 with the endpoint that requests `eth0` named
`eth0`, and some respond with an error that the name is in use. This holds whatever the
names of the container and of its networks.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-PATTERN"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-PATTERN**: A requested name with %d is accepted

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE](#NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with an endpoint that requests an interface name that contains `%d`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created container with such an endpoint responds
204, and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running container with such an endpoint
responds 200. The container then has an interface on the network.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-NAME-KERNEL-REWRITE**: A requested name with %d is accepted, and the kernel numbers it

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED) · *Concerns:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-PATTERN](#NET-IFACE-NAME-PATTERN) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME](#REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME)

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created container with an endpoint that requests an
interface name that contains `%d` responds 204, and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for
a running container with such an endpoint responds 200. The kernel gives the interface the first
free name that matches, such as `eth0`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED-WINDOWS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED-WINDOWS**: On Windows, a container whose endpoint requests an interface name starts

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* os-windows · *Platforms:* windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED](#NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED)

*Applies to:* Windows nodes with a created or stopped container with an endpoint that requests
an interface name

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 204. `GET
/containers/{id}/json` then reports `State.Running` true, and a non-empty
`EndpointID` for the network.

<a id="NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-WINDOWS-NAME-IGNORED**: On Windows, the interface does not get the requested ifname

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Concerns:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED-WINDOWS](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REQUESTED-WINDOWS) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED)

*Applies to:* A Windows container with an endpoint whose
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` names a name other than the one that Windows gives
the interface

The container's interface on that network does not have the requested name.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT**: An interface without a requested name is named eth<N>

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT](#REQ-NET-IFACE-NAME-DEFAULT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with an endpoint that does not request an interface name, on a network
of a built-in driver without `com.docker.network.container_iface_prefix`

The interface name is `eth<N>`. When the endpoint is the container's only endpoint, the
name is `eth0`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START"></a>

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-CLI**: docker run -d with a refused interface name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run -d` with a `com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that the OS refuses
