<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-UNCHECKED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-UNCHECKED**: An interface name that the OS refuses is not checked at create or connect

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST)

`POST /containers/create` for a container with an endpoint whose
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` has 16 characters or more responds 201.
`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a created or stopped container, with such an endpoint,
responds 200. Only `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container refuses the endpoint.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-CLI**: docker network connect with a refused interface name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`docker network connect` for the container, with a
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that the OS refuses, exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START**: A container whose endpoints request one name, or lo, does not start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *Exact form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with two endpoints that request
the same interface name, or with an endpoint that requests `lo`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT**: A connect requesting lo or an existing interface name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *Exact form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT](#NET-API-FAILED-CONNECT-IFACE-LEFT), [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an endpoint that requests
`lo`, responds with a 4xx or 5xx status. It does the same with an endpoint that requests
the name of one of the container's interfaces.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500**: A duplicate interface name or lo at start responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START) · *Pins:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a created or stopped container with two endpoints that request
the same interface name, or with one that requests `lo`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that names
the interface.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500**: A connect requesting lo or an existing name responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT) · *Pins:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` for the container, with an endpoint that requests
`lo` or the name of one of its interfaces, responds 500. The message names the
interface.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-CLI**: docker run -d with a duplicate interface name or lo fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`docker run -d` exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error when two of the container's
endpoints request the same interface name. It does the same when an endpoint requests
`lo`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED**: Interface-name conflicts are not checked at container create

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST)

At API version 1.44 or later, `POST /containers/create` for a
container with two endpoints that request the same interface name responds 201. So does a
request for a container with an endpoint that requests `lo`. Only `POST
/containers/{id}/start` refuses the container.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-CLI**: docker network connect requesting lo or an existing name fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container

`docker network connect` for the container exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error
when the endpoint requests `lo` or the name of one of its interfaces.

<a id="NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-HTTP500-REFUSED**: Refused disconnect and ifname requests respond 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-HTTP500) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED), [NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500](#NET-API-DISCONNECT-NOT-ATTACHED-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-CONNECT-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START), [NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-CONFLICT-START-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START), [NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-HTTP500](#NET-IFACE-NAME-REFUSED-START-HTTP500) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS)

Each request below is refused, and responds 500: (1) `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect`
for a container that is not attached to the network. (2) On a Linux node, `POST
/containers/{id}/start` and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for an endpoint with a
`com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname` that the OS refuses, that is `lo`, or that
is the name of an interface that the container already has or that another of its endpoints
requests.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS**: A standalone container's interface has its requested static address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With IPv6 disabled on its interface, a static IPv6 address is dropped ([NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED))

*Applies to:* A running standalone container whose endpoint on a network has an
`IPv4Address` or `IPv6Address` in `IPAMConfig`

Its interface on that network has that address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT**: A requested static address is reported in the container's settings

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With IPv6 disabled on its interface, a static IPv6 address is dropped ([NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED))

*Applies to:* A running standalone container whose endpoint on a network has an
`IPv4Address` or `IPv6Address` in `IPAMConfig`

`GET /containers/{id}/json` reports the address as `IPAddress` or
`GlobalIPv6Address` in `NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-RESTART"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-RESTART**: A standalone container gets its static address again when it starts again

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With IPv6 disabled on its interface, a static IPv6 address is dropped ([NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED))

*Applies to:* A stopped standalone container that has run, whose endpoint on a network has an
`IPv4Address` or `IPv6Address` in `IPAMConfig`, while no other
endpoint on the network has that address

After `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 204, its interface on
that network has that address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-IPV6-DISABLED**: With IPv6 disabled on its interface, a static IPv6 address is dropped

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS), [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-INSPECT), [NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-RESTART](#NET-IFACE-STATIC-ADDRESS-RESTART) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-STATIC-ADDRESS)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped standalone container whose endpoint on a network has an
`IPv6Address` in `IPAMConfig`, and that has
`net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6` set to 1 in `HostConfig.Sysctls`, or
`net.ipv6.conf.IFNAME.disable_ipv6=1` in that endpoint's
`com.docker.network.endpoint.sysctls`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 204. Its interface on that
network then has no IPv6 address, and `GET /containers/{id}/json` reports no
`GlobalIPv6Address` in `NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS**: A container's interface has the link-local addresses that it requests

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS) · *CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-CLI](#NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container whose endpoint on a network has addresses in
`IPAMConfig.LinkLocalIPs`, from its create or from a later connect. An IPv6 address
among them is for a network with `EnableIPv6` true.

The container's interface on that network has each of those addresses.

<a id="NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS-CLI**: docker run and docker network connect apply --link-local-ip

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* cli, os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS) · *CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS](#NET-IFACE-LINK-LOCAL-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a network that is not Swarm-scoped, and an address in
`169.254.0.0/16`, or in `fe80::/10` when the network has IPv6 enabled

`docker run -d` with `--network` naming the network and
`--link-local-ip` set to the address exits zero. The container's interface on the
network then has the address. `docker network connect` for a running container, with
`--link-local-ip` set to the address, does the same.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE**: An endpoint MacAddress set at create is the interface's MAC address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A running container created at API version 1.44 or later with an endpoint
`MacAddress` on a network whose driver accepts an endpoint MAC address

Its interface on that network has that MAC address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT**: An endpoint MacAddress set at connect is the interface's MAC address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network whose driver accepts an endpoint MAC address

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` with `MacAddress` set, at API version
1.54 or later, responds 200, the container's interface on the network has that MAC address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION**: Before API 1.54, a connect ignores MacAddress

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE), [REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network whose driver accepts an endpoint MAC address,
and a `MacAddress` other than the one that the driver gives the interface when no
`MacAddress` is set

At API versions before 1.54, after `POST /networks/{id}/connect` with
`MacAddress` set responds 200, the container's interface on the network does not have
that MAC address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION**: Before API 1.44, a create ignores an endpoint's MacAddress

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE), [REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS](#REQ-NET-ENDPOINT-MAC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE](#NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE), [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

*Applies to:* A network whose driver accepts an endpoint MAC address, and a
`MacAddress` other than the one that the driver gives the interface when no
`MacAddress` is set

At API versions before 1.44, `POST /containers/create` that sets `MacAddress`
in the endpoint settings of that network, and does not set the container-wide
`MacAddress`, responds 201. Once the container runs, its interface on the network
does not have that MAC address.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT**: A connect with MacAddress fails where the driver does not accept it

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *Exact form:* [IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT-HTTP500) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC) · *Concerned by:* [IPVL-NETIF-HTTP500-REFUSED](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-HTTP500-REFUSED)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network whose driver does not accept an endpoint MAC
address

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network, for the container, with
`MacAddress` set, at API version 1.54 or later, responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.
`GET /networks/{id}` then does not list the container.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START**: A container with a MacAddress its driver refuses does not start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT](#REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT) · *Exact form:* [IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-HTTP500](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC) · *Concerned by:* [IPVL-NETIF-HTTP500-REFUSED](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-NETIF-HTTP500-REFUSED), [IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-UNCHECKED](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-OPT-MAC-ADDRESS-UNCHECKED)

*Applies to:* A network whose driver does not accept an endpoint MAC address, and a created
container without `HostConfig.AutoRemove`, created at API version 1.44 or later,
whose endpoint on that network sets `MacAddress`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.
`GET /containers/{id}/json` then reports `State.Status` as `created`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI**: docker run -d with --mac-address fails where the driver refuses it

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Assumes:* [NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC](#NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC)

`docker run -d` with `--mac-address` and with `--network` naming a
network whose driver does not accept an endpoint MAC address exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-CREATED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-CREATED**: Creating a macvlan network on a missing VLAN parent creates the sub-interface

*Observed from:* api, node · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT](#REQ-NET-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [NET-HOST-VLAN](#NET-HOST-VLAN) · *Does not cover:* A macvlan VLAN parent on an interface whose name has a dot responds 500 ([NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED))

*Applies to:* An interface `<interface>` on the node other than `lo`, and a VLAN ID
from 1 to 4094 that no 802.1Q VLAN link on `<interface>` has, where `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`
has at most 15 characters, is not an interface of the node, and is not the `parent` of
another `macvlan` network

`POST /networks/create` for a `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, that
uses the default IPAM driver, whose `parent` is `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, and whose
`macvlan_mode` is unset, empty, `bridge`, `private`, `passthru` or `vepa`,
responds 201. The node then has an interface `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`: a VLAN link on
`<interface>` with that VLAN ID.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED**: Deleting a macvlan network deletes the VLAN parent that its create added

*Observed from:* api, node · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [NET-HOST-VLAN](#NET-HOST-VLAN) · *Concerned by:* [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-IPVLAN](#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-IPVLAN)

*Applies to:* A `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, without containers, whose
create added its `parent` `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, where no other `macvlan`
network and no `ipvlan` network on the node, including a Swarm-scoped one that the node
has a local attachment to, has that `parent`

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 204. The node then does not have the
interface `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-IPVLAN"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED-IPVLAN**: Deleting a macvlan network removes a VLAN parent an ipvlan network uses

*Observed from:* api, node, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [IPVL-HOST-IPVLAN](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-HOST-IPVLAN), [IPVL-HOST-VLAN](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-HOST-VLAN), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [NET-HOST-VLAN](#NET-HOST-VLAN) · *Concerns:* [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED](#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-REMOVED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAITHFUL](../principles.md#PRIN-FAITHFUL)

*Applies to:* A `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, without containers, whose
create added its `parent` `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, where no other `macvlan`
network on the node has that `parent`, and an `ipvlan` network that is not
Swarm-scoped, with that `parent` and a running container

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the macvlan network responds 204. The node then does not
have the interface `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, and the container has no interface on the ipvlan
network, while `GET /networks/{id}` for the ipvlan network still lists the container.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-KEPT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-KEPT**: Deleting a macvlan network keeps a VLAN parent that existed before it

*Observed from:* api, node · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-OWNS-ONLY-ITS-OWN](../principles.md#PRIN-OWNS-ONLY-ITS-OWN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [NET-HOST-VLAN](#NET-HOST-VLAN)

*Applies to:* A `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, without containers, whose
`parent` is a VLAN sub-interface `<interface>.<VLAN ID>` that existed before the
network was created and that no `macvlan` network's create added

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 204. The node then still has the
interface `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-REMOVED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-REMOVED**: Deleting a macvlan network without a parent removes what its create added

*Observed from:* api, node · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-DUMMY](#NET-HOST-DUMMY), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, created without a
`parent`, without containers

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 204. The node then has no interface
that the network's create added.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-ISOLATED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-ISOLATED**: A container on a macvlan network without a parent reaches nothing outside it

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-INTERNAL](#REQ-NET-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-INTERNAL) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-DUMMY](#NET-HOST-DUMMY), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-MACVLAN](#NET-HOST-MACVLAN), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container attached only to a `macvlan` network that was created without
a `parent`

The container cannot reach addresses outside that network, including every address of the node.

<a id="NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-SAME-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-SAME-NETWORK**: Containers on a macvlan network without a parent reach each other

*Observed from:* ctr → ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-INTERNAL](#REQ-NET-MACVLAN-NO-PARENT-INTERNAL) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-DUMMY](#NET-HOST-DUMMY), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-MACVLAN](#NET-HOST-MACVLAN), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Two containers attached to a `macvlan` network that was created without a
`parent`, with `macvlan_mode` unset, empty or `bridge`

Each container reaches the other at that container's address on the network.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NO-MACVLAN"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NO-MACVLAN**: Without macvlan links, starting a macvlan container responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [NET-HOST-MACVLAN](#NET-HOST-MACVLAN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A Linux host whose kernel does not offer macvlan links, and a created or stopped
container with an endpoint on a `macvlan` network

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that
contains `failed to create the macvlan port`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN**: Without VLAN links, creating a macvlan network on a VLAN parent responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [NET-HOST-VLAN](#NET-HOST-VLAN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A macvlan VLAN parent on an interface whose name has a dot responds 500 ([NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED](#NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED))

*Applies to:* A Linux host whose kernel does not offer VLAN links, an existing interface
`<interface>`, and a VLAN ID from 1 to 4094, where `<interface>.<VLAN ID>` is not an
interface of the node and is not the `parent` of another `macvlan` network

`POST /networks/create` for a `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, that
uses the default IPAM driver, whose `parent` is `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, and whose
`macvlan_mode` is unset, empty, `bridge`, `private`, `passthru` or `vepa`,
responds 500, with a message that contains `vlan link`.

<a id="NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-IFACE-STACKED-VLAN-PARENT-REFUSED**: A macvlan VLAN parent on an interface whose name has a dot responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-CREATED](#NET-IFACE-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT-CREATED), [NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN](#NET-IFACE-NO-VLAN) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT](#REQ-NET-MACVLAN-VLAN-PARENT)

*Applies to:* An interface `<interface>` of the node whose name contains a dot, such as a VLAN
sub-interface, and a name `<interface>.<VLAN ID>` that is not an interface of the node and is
not the `parent` of another `macvlan` network

`POST /networks/create` for a `macvlan` network that is not Swarm-scoped, that
uses the default IPAM driver, whose `parent` is `<interface>.<VLAN ID>`, and whose
`macvlan_mode` is unset, empty, `bridge`, `private`, `passthru` or `vepa`,
responds 500, with a message that contains `required interface name format is:
name.vlan_id`. `GET /networks` then does not list a network with the request's
`Name`.

<a id="network-common-default-gateway"></a>

## Default gateway

<a id="NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS**: A container on internal networks only cannot reach addresses outside them

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS) · *Exact form:* [NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY](#NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A Windows container on internal overlays only reaches outside addresses ([NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS))

*Applies to:* A container attached only to `internal` networks, whose routes are the routes
that the daemon gives it

The container cannot reach addresses outside the subnets of those networks.

<a id="NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY**: The daemon gives a container on internal networks only no default route

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A Windows container on internal overlays only reaches outside addresses ([NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS))

*Applies to:* A container attached only to `internal` networks

The daemon does not give the container a default route.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-GW-PRIORITY**: The default route goes through the endpoint with the highest GwPriority

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY](#REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with endpoints on two or more networks that are not
`internal`, one with a higher `GwPriority` than the others

For each IP version that the endpoint gives the container a gateway or default route for, the
container's default route goes through that endpoint.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-TIE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-GW-PRIORITY-TIE**: With equal GwPriority, the default route follows a fixed endpoint order

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY](#REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with endpoints on two or more networks that are not
`internal`, all with the same `GwPriority`

For each IP version, the container's default route is through the first endpoint that gives a
gateway or default route for that version, in this order: (1) endpoints that give one for both
IPv4 and IPv6, then endpoints that give one for a single version; (2) within each group, network
names in byte order.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-GW-PRIORITY-IGNORED-CREATE**: At API version 1.47 or earlier, container create ignores GwPriority

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE), [REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY](#REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Two networks that are not `internal` and that each give a container a default
route, where a container with endpoints on both and the same `GwPriority` for each
has its default route through the first

At API version 1.47 or earlier, `POST /containers/create` with endpoints on both
networks in `EndpointsConfig`, and a `GwPriority` higher than 0 for the
endpoint on the second, responds 201. `GET /containers/{id}/json` then reports
`GwPriority` 0 for each of the container's networks. On Linux nodes, once the
container runs, its default route goes through the first network.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT**: From API 1.48, a connect applies GwPriority

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY](#REQ-NET-GW-PRIORITY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT-API-VERSION](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT-API-VERSION)

At API version 1.48 or later, after `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running
container with `GwPriority` set responds 200, `GET /containers/{id}/json`
reports that `GwPriority` for the network. On Linux nodes, when that value is higher
than the `GwPriority` of the container's other endpoints, the container's default
route goes through the new endpoint, for each IP version that the endpoint gives a gateway or
default route for.

<a id="NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT-API-VERSION"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT-API-VERSION**: Before API 1.48, a connect applies GwPriority too

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT](#NET-GW-PRIORITY-CONNECT) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE)

At API version 1.47 or earlier, after `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running
container with `GwPriority` set responds 200, `GET /containers/{id}/json`
reports that `GwPriority` for the network. On Linux nodes, when that value is higher
than the `GwPriority` of the container's other endpoints, the container's default
route goes through the new endpoint, for each IP version that the endpoint gives a gateway or
default route for.

<a id="network-common-default-gateway-in-a-swarm"></a>

### In a Swarm

<a id="NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS**: A Windows container on internal overlays only reaches outside addresses

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-windows · *Platforms:* windows

*Pinned by:* [NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-ROUTE](#NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-ROUTE) · *Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY](#NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY), [NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#NET-GW-INTERNAL-ONLY-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-EGRESS-INTERNAL-ONLY](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EGRESS-INTERNAL-ONLY) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#REQ-NET-INTERNAL-NO-EXTERNAL-ACCESS), [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS](swarm-traffic.md#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-EGRESS)

A Windows container attached only to `internal` overlays reaches addresses outside those
networks.

<a id="NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-ROUTE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-ROUTE**: A Windows container on internal overlays only has a default route

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* os-windows · *Platforms:* windows

*Pins:* [NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS](#NET-GW-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-OVERLAY-EGRESS) · *Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

A Windows container attached only to `internal` overlays has a default route.

<a id="network-common-file-etc-hosts"></a>

## `/etc/hosts`

In this section, a container's addresses on a network are the IPv4 address and the IPv6 address that
`GET /containers/{id}/json` reports for that network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`, as `IPAddress` and `GlobalIPv6Address`.
The addresses in `IPAMConfig.LinkLocalIPs`, and the link-local addresses that the kernel
assigns, are not among them. The container's addresses are its addresses on each of its networks.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES**: /etc/hosts maps each of the container's addresses to its hostname

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A container that does not use the host's network

For each of the container's addresses, `/etc/hosts` has a line that maps the address to
the container's hostname. The exceptions are addresses on the ingress network and on
`docker_gwbridge`. IPv6 addresses are also exceptions while IPv6 is disabled in the
container, so that its loopback interface does not have an IPv6 address, for example with
`net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6` set to 1.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-LOCALHOST"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-LOCALHOST**: /etc/hosts maps the loopback addresses to localhost

*Observed from:* task, ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A container that does not use the host's network

`/etc/hosts` has a line that maps `127.0.0.1` to `localhost`. It also has a line that
maps `::1` to `localhost`, except while IPv6 is disabled in the container, as for
[*NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES*](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-DOMAIN-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-DOMAIN-NAME**: A dotted hostname or a domain gives full and short names in /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-FQDN](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-FQDN) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose `Hostname` contains a dot, or that has a
`Domainname`

Each line for the container's addresses gives two names. The first is the full name: the
hostname, then a dot and the domain name if the container has one. The second is the part of the
hostname before its first dot.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-CONNECT**: A connect adds the container's addresses on the network to /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container, and a network other than the ingress network and
`docker_gwbridge`

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to that network for the container responds 200,
`/etc/hosts` has the lines for the container's addresses on that network. IPv6 addresses
are exceptions while IPv6 is disabled in the container, as for [*NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES*](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-DISCONNECT**: A disconnect removes the network's addresses from /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-OWN-NAME) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a network, from its start or from a later
connect

After `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container responds 200,
`/etc/hosts` does not have the lines for the container's addresses on that network.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS**: An ExtraHosts entry adds a line to /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS](#REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS) · *CLI form:* [NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI](#NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

An entry `<name>:<address>` in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts` adds a line to
`/etc/hosts` that maps `<address>` to `<name>`. IPv6 addresses are exceptions while
IPv6 is disabled in the container, as for [*NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES*](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI**: docker run --add-host adds a line to /etc/hosts

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS](#REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS) · *CLI form of:* [NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS](#NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

`docker run -d` with `--add-host` `<name>:<address>` exits zero. The
container's `/etc/hosts` then has a line that maps `<address>` to `<name>`. IPv6
addresses are exceptions while IPv6 is disabled in the container, as for
[*NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES*](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY**: A host-gateway entry maps to each address in host-gateway-ips

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOST-GATEWAY](#REQ-NET-HOST-GATEWAY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

*Applies to:* A daemon with `host-gateway-ips` set

An entry `<name>:host-gateway` in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts` adds a line to
`/etc/hosts` for each address in `host-gateway-ips`. Each line maps the
address to `<name>`. IPv6 addresses are exceptions while IPv6 is disabled in the container, as
for [*NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES*](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: Without host-gateway-ips, host-gateway is the default bridge's addresses

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOST-GATEWAY](#REQ-NET-HOST-GATEWAY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

*Applies to:* A daemon without `host-gateway-ips`

An entry `<name>:host-gateway` in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts` adds a line to
`/etc/hosts` for the default bridge's own IPv4 address, and one for its IPv6 address if it
has one: the `Gateway` values that `GET /networks/{id}` for the network
`bridge` reports in `IPAM.Config`. This holds whatever networks the
container is attached to. IPv6 addresses are exceptions while IPv6 is disabled in the container,
as for [*NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES*](#NET-HOSTS-ADDRESSES).

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-ADDRESS-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-ADDRESS-CREATE**: Without a host-gateway address, a host-gateway entry is accepted without a warning

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD)

*Applies to:* A daemon without a host-gateway address: a Linux daemon without
`host-gateway-ips` and with `bridge` set to `none`, or a Windows
daemon without `host-gateway-ips`

`POST /containers/create` for a container with an entry `<name>:host-gateway` in
`HostConfig.ExtraHosts` responds 201 without a warning about the host-gateway entry.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE**: Without a host-gateway address, the container does not start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT](#REQ-NET-START-FAILED-CONTAINER-KEPT) · *Exact form:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-HTTP500](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With live-restored containers, the daemon's default-bridge settings are not applied ([BR-OPT-DAEMON-LIVE-RESTORE-UNAPPLIED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-DAEMON-LIVE-RESTORE-UNAPPLIED)) · *Concerned by:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-ADDRESS-CREATE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-ADDRESS-CREATE)

*Applies to:* A daemon without a host-gateway address (on a Linux node, one without
`host-gateway-ips` and with `bridge` set to `none`; on a Windows
node, one without `host-gateway-ips`), and a created container without
`HostConfig.AutoRemove` and with an entry `<name>:host-gateway` in
`HostConfig.ExtraHosts`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.
`GET /containers/{id}/json` then reports `State.Status` as `created`.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-HTTP500**: Without a host-gateway address, starting the container responds 500

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With live-restored containers, the daemon's default-bridge settings are not applied ([BR-OPT-DAEMON-LIVE-RESTORE-UNAPPLIED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-DAEMON-LIVE-RESTORE-UNAPPLIED))

*Applies to:* A daemon without a host-gateway address (on a Linux node, one without
`host-gateway-ips` and with `bridge` set to `none`; on a Windows
node, one without `host-gateway-ips`), and a created container with an entry
`<name>:host-gateway` in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts`

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that
contains `unable to derive the IP value for host-gateway`.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE-CLI**: docker run with --add-host <name>:host-gateway and no address fails

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED) · *CLI form of:* [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-NO-BRIDGE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With live-restored containers, the daemon's default-bridge settings are not applied ([BR-OPT-DAEMON-LIVE-RESTORE-UNAPPLIED](bridge-networking.md#BR-OPT-DAEMON-LIVE-RESTORE-UNAPPLIED))

*Applies to:* A daemon without a host-gateway address (on a Linux node, one without
`host-gateway-ips` and with `bridge` set to `none`; on a Windows
node, one without `host-gateway-ips`)

`docker run` with `--add-host` `<name>:host-gateway` exits non-zero and prints the
daemon's error.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED**: On Windows, extra hosts entries are accepted and not written to the hosts file

*Observed from:* api, ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerns:* [NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS](#NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS), [NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI](#NET-HOSTS-EXTRA-HOSTS-CLI), [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY), [NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#NET-HOSTS-HOST-GATEWAY-DEFAULT-BRIDGE), [NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES](#NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS](#REQ-NET-EXTRA-HOSTS), [REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES)

`POST /containers/create` with entries in `HostConfig.ExtraHosts`
responds 201. Once the container runs, its hosts file has no line for those entries. In the
hosts file of each task of a service whose `ContainerSpec.Hosts` has entries, no
line has those entries.

<a id="network-common-file-etc-hosts-in-a-swarm"></a>

### In a Swarm

<a id="NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES**: A task's /etc/hosts maps each alias of a Hosts entry to its address

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A task's /etc/hosts drops the aliases of a Hosts entry ([NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED](#NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED)) · *Concerned by:* [NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED](#NET-HOSTS-WINDOWS-EXTRA-HOSTS-IGNORED)

*Applies to:* A service whose `ContainerSpec.Hosts` has an entry `<address> <name>
<alias>...` with one or more aliases

In the `/etc/hosts` of each task of the service, `<address>` maps to `<name>` and to
each alias.

<a id="NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES-DROPPED**: A task's /etc/hosts drops the aliases of a Hosts entry

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES](#NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ALIASES) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES](#REQ-NET-HOSTS-SERVICE-ENTRIES)

*Applies to:* A service whose `ContainerSpec.Hosts` has an entry
`<address> <name> <alias>...` with one or more aliases

In the `/etc/hosts` of each task of the service, `<address>` maps to `<name>` only,
and no line has the aliases.

<a id="network-common-driver-properties"></a>

## Driver properties

Expectations in this spec name a property of a network driver, not the driver itself, where the set
of drivers with the property can change. The two detectors below give the properties of the built-in
drivers. A plugin driver has the properties that it implements. The expectations hold for the
`l2tunnel` and `ics` drivers on a Windows node where `POST /networks/create`
for a network of that driver responds 201.

<a id="NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-DRVPROP-ADDS-INTERFACE**: Every built-in driver but host and null adds an interface

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [BR-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [IPVL-HOST-IPVLAN](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-HOST-IPVLAN), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-MACVLAN](#NET-HOST-MACVLAN), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Assumed by:* [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION) · *Rationale:* Driver properties decide a container's interfaces and its MAC requests ([RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS](#RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS))

A container on a network of one of these drivers has an interface on the network:

- `bridge`
- `overlay`
- `macvlan`
- `ipvlan`
- Windows: `nat`, `transparent`, `l2bridge`, `l2tunnel`, `ics`, `internal`, `private`

A container on a network of one of these drivers does not:

- `host`
- `null` (the `none` network)

<a id="NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC"></a>

**Expectation (detector) NET-DRVPROP-ENDPOINT-MAC**: Built-in drivers that add an interface accept a MAC, except ipvlan

*Observed from:* api, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [BR-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](bridge-networking.md#BR-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [IPVL-HOST-IPVLAN](ipvlan-networking.md#IPVL-HOST-IPVLAN), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-MACVLAN](#NET-HOST-MACVLAN), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Assumed by:* [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CONNECT-API-VERSION), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-CREATE-API-VERSION), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-CONNECT), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START), [NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI](#NET-IFACE-MAC-ADDRESS-REFUSED-START-CLI) · *Rationale:* Driver properties decide a container's interfaces and its MAC requests ([RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS](#RAT-NET-DRIVER-PROPERTY-SETS))

These drivers accept an endpoint MAC address:

- `bridge`
- `overlay`
- `macvlan`
- Windows: `nat`, `transparent`, `l2bridge`, `l2tunnel`, `ics`, `internal`, `private`

These drivers do not accept one:

- `ipvlan`

For these drivers, the property does not apply, because they add no interface:

- `host`
- `null` (the `none` network)

<a id="network-common-daemon-restart"></a>

## Daemon restart

<a id="NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED**: After SIGKILL and restart, the daemon's old namespaces are removed

*Observed from:* node · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

After `SIGKILL` and restart, every network namespace that the daemon created before the
kill is removed, other than an overlay network's namespace and the namespace of a container that
live-restore keeps running. This includes the namespaces of load-balancer and ingress sandboxes,
and of containers that the daemon does not keep running. An overlay network's namespace is the
one that holds the network's VXLAN device. A namespace that the daemon creates after the restart
is a different namespace, even at the same path. A namespace is removed once no mount of it
remains in the mount namespace that the daemon runs in, even while a process still runs in it or
another mount namespace keeps a copy of a mount of it.

<a id="NET-RESTART-LIVE-RESTORE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) NET-RESTART-LIVE-RESTORE**: With live-restore, a container keeps its namespace and interfaces

*Observed from:* node, ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-LIVE-RESTORE](#REQ-NET-LIVE-RESTORE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a running container, whose daemon has `live-restore`
true

After `SIGKILL` and restart, the container keeps its network namespace and its
interfaces.
